neet_che_u20_t07_1.working: Brisk effervescence with dilute acid means a carbonate. The CO2 released turns lime water milky because CaCO3 forms.

neet_che_u20_t07_2.working: In [Fe(H2O)5NO]2+ the NO is bound as NO+, so x + 1 = +2 and x = +1. This is the textbook assignment; the true electronic structure is debated.

neet_che_u20_t07_3.working: This is the chromyl chloride test. Orange-red CrO2Cl2 vapours give yellow Na2CrO4 in NaOH, which precipitates yellow PbCrO4 with lead acetate. The anion is Cl-.

neet_che_u20_t07_4.working: S2- gives violet with nitroprusside (I). NO2- liberates I2 so KI-starch turns blue (II). SO4 2- gives BaSO4, insoluble in conc. HCl (III). I- gives a violet CCl4 layer with Cl2 water (IV).

neet_che_u20_t07_5.working: A is true: AgCl is white and dissolves in NH4OH. B is false: AgI is practically insoluble in NH4OH. C is true: nitrite interferes and is destroyed by sulphamic acid. D is true: Br2 vapours are reddish-brown. E is false: BaSO4 is insoluble in conc. HCl. So A, C and D are correct.
